customer_question: The A2DP/SNK/SYN test case isn't available in PTS and can't be executed - since it's Test Case Category D, is it acceptable to leave it un-executed?
question_variants: Is a Test Case Category D item that's missing from PTS required for Profile testing?
What do we do when a PTS-listed test case can't actually be executed in the PTS tool?
Can Category D test cases be excluded from the Profile test report?
actual_issue: During [COMPANY]'s Profile testing, the A2DP/SNK/SYN test case was not available as an executable item in PTS. The tester asked whether, since this test case falls under Test Case Category D, it is acceptable to leave it un-executed.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth qualification test cases are grouped into categories (e.g., Mandatory vs Optional/Category D). If a particular test case is categorized as 'D' (not mandatory) and the PTS tool doesn't actually provide a way to execute it, it is acceptable to leave that item un-executed and out of scope for the test report.
consultant_answer: Yes, that's correct - execution of this test case is not mandatory (Test Case Category D), so if PTS doesn't provide a way to test it, it is out of scope and can be left un-executed.
decision_logic: If a test case is categorized as Category D (non-mandatory) per the ICS/test plan, and PTS does not provide an executable test for it, it can be excluded from the test report without issue.
final_recommendation: For test cases missing from PTS, check the test case category in the ICS/test plan; if it is Category D (non-mandatory), exclude it from the report as out of scope.
risk_if_done_wrong: Treating a mandatory test case as exempt simply because PTS lacks it could leave a required test unperformed and undocumented in the final report, risking certification issues; conversely, unnecessarily trying to force-execute a non-mandatory test that PTS can't run wastes time.
